clue.text: Charm one's way in

explanation.surface: Someone talks their way into a place with charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to captivate them, and a doorway is the way into a building.

clue.text: Name after former wife, to cause a stir

indicators.note: after places the naming word behind the former wife in the answer

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, here a former wife
to cite someone is to name them, as in court or a list

explanation.surface: A divorcee's name being mentioned sets tongues wagging.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse or stimulate people is to make a commotion among them.

clue.text: Dresses-there's a stack in the back street!

indicators.note: in places the haystack inside the turned street letters
back tells us the street abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: A remark about clothes and a haystack sitting in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round before 'in' takes the stack. To trick out or trick up is an old phrase for dressing someone finely.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick out is to adorn or deck in finery, so it is a synonym of clothes as a verb.

clue.text: Vigilant fellow had his eyes on the peacock's tail

definitions.text: Vigilant fellow had his eyes on the peacock's tail

parts.words: Vigilant fellow had his eyes on the peacock's tail
parts.note: in Greek myth the hundred-eyed watchman was slain and Hera set his eyes on the peacock's tail

explanation.surface: A watchful man keeps staring at a peacock's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man ogling a bird; the myth says the giant's eyes were literally placed on the peacock's tail by Hera.
explanation.definitionFit: The hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth gives his name to any watchful guardian.

clue.text: Study the route and make a line on the map

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a tour is a route taken round places

explanation.surface: Planning a journey by studying the route and marking the map.
explanation.definitionFit: Contour lines join points of equal height on a survey chart.

clue.text: Goes around in women's clothes

explanation.surface: Someone goes out dressed in women's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to pass round its edge, and the garments hang from the waist.

clue.text: Bird which makes the cat sit up and take notice!

definitions.text: Bird which makes the cat sit up and take notice!

parts.words: Bird which makes the cat sit up and take notice!
parts.note: a pet name for a cat followed by a word for alert splits the gull's name into two parts

explanation.surface: A bird that makes the household cat suddenly alert.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as KITTI (kitty, a cat) plus WAKE (awake): a cat that has sat up and taken notice.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small cliff-nesting gull of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Read about a young chap noted for having thought things out

indicators.note: about means the reading word goes round the young chap and his note

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a young male child
noted means given a note, the musical note E

explanation.surface: Someone reads about a young man famous for his careful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' is the odd piece: a young chap given a note, the musical note E, and the whole goes inside the reading word, which 'about' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Argued logically: a conclusion worked through step by step is a considered one.

clue.text: Sis cross when they cut her up!

definitions.text: Sis cross when they cut her up!

indicators.note: cut up suggests the letters of the two words are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sister is angry when someone cuts her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' (with 'cut') signals the anagram of SIS CROSS; the whole clue also describes the blades doing the cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue as a whole pictures the cutting tool snipping, so the entire sentence defines it.

clue.text: Hanging on to a large number of fish surrounding trap

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

indicators.note: surrounding means the fish goes round the snare

parts.note: the ling is a long cod-like fish
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: Lots of fish are caught around a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding tightly to something is gripping it fast.

clue.text: The way a returning sailor and I see grey clouds

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: returning means the sailor word is read backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor coming home with a friend notices grey clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: These are low flat layered sheets of cloud, often dull grey overcast.

clue.text: Get the bird when bringing other birds back

indicators.note: bringing back means the word for those seabirds is turned round

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots

explanation.surface: Someone gets booed when bringing back other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' sounds like being booed, but 'bird' is the definition. 'back' turns AUKS round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large predatory seabird of the gull family that robs other birds.

clue.text: What the shop lifter might do to case the joint

definitions.text: What the shop lifter might do

explanation.surface: A shoplifter sizes up a store before robbing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief would steal goods from the shelves, and to case a place is to assess or review the situation.

clue.text: Images in solid form

indicators.note: form tells us the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: Pictures rendered in a solid form, like statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Graven images are objects of worship, such as carved statues of gods.

clue.text: Overcook the fish perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone burns the fish they are cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch food is to burn its surface; the other sense is a trout-like lake fish.

clue.text: Worker strikes when these restrict his power

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
cuffs are blows or slaps

explanation.surface: A workman goes on strike when his power is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' looks like industrial action but means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Manacles lock the wrists and so limit what a prisoner can do.

clue.text: Perplex a mature enthusiast

indicators.note: to perplex is to muddle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Confusing a grown-up fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional devotee pursues a pastime out of love for it.

clue.text: Mysterious secret ten cooked up

indicators.note: cooked up means invented or concocted, so the letters are remade

parts.note: IO looks like the figure 10

explanation.surface: A secret plan hatched by ten conspirators.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure knowledge understood only by an inner circle is arcane.

clue.text: The point in ecclesiastical preferment is to create big guns

indicators.note: in puts the compass point within the church office

parts.note: the office of a canon in a cathedral chapter is a church appointment
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The real aim of church promotion is to produce heavyweights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big guns' looks like important people but means artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy artillery pieces collectively make up the weaponry.

clue.text: Firm stem

explanation.surface: A sturdy stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal and steadfast describes a firm ally; to stop a flow of blood is the other sense.

clue.text: Song sounds as though it wasn't written for a lady

indicators.note: sounds as though says the word for a man is heard rather than seen

parts.words: it wasn't written for a lady
parts.note: a piece for a man is for him rather than her

explanation.surface: A song apparently not composed for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song of praise sung in church.

clue.text: A cheap fares scheme has point

explanation.surface: A budget ticket offer has a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance Purchase Excursion was a discounted ticket type; the other sense is the summit or tip.

clue.text: Girl you said was allowed to have a little ring

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: said shows the word is spoken, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: the word you is heard as the letter U
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A girl, you claim, was permitted a small ring.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small band or fillet, as on a column, so a small circle.

clue.text: Appropriate headgear for a rowing man

definitions.text: Appropriate headgear for a rowing man

parts.words: Appropriate headgear for a rowing man
parts.note: a flat straw hat shares its name with someone who goes out in a small craft

explanation.walkthrough: The flat straw hat traditionally worn at regattas is named for someone who goes boating.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff straw hat with a flat crown, linked with rowing regattas.

clue.text: Grave cart?

explanation.surface: A cart for carrying the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient burial mound is one sense; a wheeled handcart is the other.

clue.text: The key note is good for you

explanation.surface: The main message is that it is healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the first note of a scale names the key; a restorative drink is also good for you.

clue.text: Somehow nominates this state

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some other order

explanation.surface: In some way this state nominates its candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Midwestern US state on the Canadian border.

clue.text: Nigel out on the town

indicators.note: out means the name is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Nigel goes for a night out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out on the town' reads as a night out, but 'out' signals the anagram and 'town' is the definition: a town in Moray, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in Moray, northeast Scotland.

clue.text: Sports day is cancelled, so go away

parts.note: a run is a race, an event at a sports day
something called off is off

explanation.surface: Sports day is called off, so everyone leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee or leave in a hurry is to depart.

clue.text: Last bomb not so heavy-just a wretched nuisance

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word bomb is taken

parts.note: lighter means weighing less

explanation.surface: A final bomb that is lighter is still a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or annoying person is called this in British slang.

clue.text: OK in bed, but most shy

indicators.note: in puts the agreement inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
yes means OK as an agreement

explanation.surface: A bashful person agrees to bed but stays modest.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bashful or demure, so the most modest.

clue.text: Laurel produced a picture of a Scottish university

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
drew means sketched or produced a picture

explanation.surface: A comic actor sketches a picture of a Scottish university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' looks like a plant but is Stan Laurel. The university at St Andrews in Fife is named after the apostle, Scotland's patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose: the university town in Fife bears the apostle's name, Scotland's patron saint.
